questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: a student claims that after rome fell, european kingdoms were run exactly like the old roman empire, just with new leaders in charge. what actually changed about how power was organised
options: power became decentralised into local feudal lordships instead of one central government
the same roman senate kept ruling but under a different name
power stayed centralised under a single emperor in rome
nothing changed at all, roman law and government continued unchanged
questions.answer: power became decentralised into local feudal lordships instead of one central government
questions.why: After Rome's central authority collapsed, there was no single ruler over Europe. Power broke into small local lordships bound by land-for-loyalty ties, which is the feudal system, not a continuation of Roman government.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: a student says a knight could ignore his lord's request for military service as long as he kept farming his land. what's wrong with this claim
options: knights owed military service to their lord in exchange for the land they held
knights had no obligations to any lord once they were granted land
knights only had to pay taxes, never fight
knights answered only to peasants working their land
questions.answer: knights owed military service to their lord in exchange for the land they held
questions.why: The feudal relationship was reciprocal: a knight (as a vassal) received land from his lord but in return owed military service. Ignoring this obligation would break the core exchange the whole system was built on.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: a student says shakespeare performed romeo and juliet exclusively for royalty in private palace theatres. what does this get wrong about his original audience
options: his plays were performed for a mixed public audience at public theatres like the globe
he only ever performed for the king and queen personally
his plays were banned from public performance entirely
his audience was made up only of wealthy nobles
questions.answer: his plays were performed for a mixed public audience at public theatres like the globe
questions.why: Shakespeare's plays were performed at public playhouses like the Globe, drawing audiences from many social classes, not just royalty or nobility performing in private.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: a student thinks shakespeare only uses metaphor in romeo and juliet, never simile. which of these lines is actually a simile, not a metaphor
options: "her beauty hangs upon the cheek of night like a rich jewel in an ethiope's ear"
"but soft, what light through yonder window breaks? it is the east, and juliet is the sun"
"it is the east, and juliet is the sun"
"juliet is the sun"
questions.answer: "her beauty hangs upon the cheek of night like a rich jewel in an ethiope's ear"
questions.why: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as', unlike a metaphor which states one thing IS another. Romeo's line comparing Juliet's beauty to a jewel using 'like' is a simile, while 'Juliet is the sun' is a metaphor.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: a student thinks the love vs hate theme is only shown through romeo and juliet's romantic dialogue. which moment instead shows the theme through violence rooted in family hatred
options: tybalt's fatal duel with mercutio, fuelled by the feud between the two families
romeo and juliet's first meeting and shared sonnet at the ball
juliet's balcony declaration of love to romeo
the friar's plan to reunite the lovers secretly
questions.answer: tybalt's fatal duel with mercutio, fuelled by the feud between the two families
questions.why: The love vs hate theme runs through conflict as much as romance. Tybalt and Mercutio's fatal duel shows how the families' hatred directly causes violence and tragedy, not just how love is expressed tenderly.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: in an experiment testing how the type of soil affects seed germination time, a student mixes up which variable is independent. what is the independent variable here
options: the type of soil used
the germination time of the seeds
the amount of water given
the temperature of the room
questions.why: The independent variable is what the experimenter deliberately changes to test its effect — here, the type of soil. Germination time is the dependent variable, the outcome being measured.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: a student claims that all mammals reproduce sexually and no mammal can reproduce asexually. is this claim accurate
options: yes, all known mammals reproduce sexually, unlike some simpler organisms that can reproduce asexually
no, several mammal species commonly reproduce asexually in the wild
no, most mammals alternate between sexual and asexual reproduction
yes, but only because mammals lack any reproductive cells
questions.answer: yes, all known mammals reproduce sexually, unlike some simpler organisms that can reproduce asexually
questions.why: Asexual reproduction (like budding or binary fission) is common in simpler organisms such as bacteria, some plants, and a few invertebrates, but no mammal species reproduces asexually — mammals rely on sexual reproduction.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: a student says the crusades had no effect on europe itself, only on the middle east. what long-term effect on european trade and towns does this overlook
options: crusades boosted trade routes and wealth in european port cities like venice and genoa
crusades destroyed all european trade routes permanently
crusades caused every european town to be abandoned
crusades had zero economic impact on any region involved
questions.answer: crusades boosted trade routes and wealth in european port cities like venice and genoa
questions.why: The Crusades increased demand for transporting and supplying armies, which enriched Italian port cities through expanded trade routes and contact with the Middle East — a major effect felt back in Europe itself.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: a student says the fall of rome only affected the city of rome itself and left the rest of the western empire's provinces functioning as before. what's wrong with this view
options: the collapse of central authority disrupted governance, trade, and infrastructure across the whole western empire
provinces outside rome were untouched and kept roman law perfectly intact
only the eastern empire was affected, not the west at all
the provinces became stronger and more unified after rome fell
questions.answer: the collapse of central authority disrupted governance, trade, and infrastructure across the whole western empire
questions.why: Rome's fall wasn't just a local event in the city — it removed the central authority that had held together government, trade networks, and infrastructure across the entire western empire, leading to widespread fragmentation.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: a student claims shakespeare wrote romeo and juliet as a comedy that was later mistakenly labelled a tragedy. what's wrong with this claim
options: shakespeare deliberately structured it as a tragedy, ending in the protagonists' deaths
the play was originally a comedy with a happy wedding ending
the tragedy label was added by victorian critics with no basis in the text
shakespeare never assigned genres to his own plays
questions.answer: shakespeare deliberately structured it as a tragedy, ending in the protagonists' deaths
questions.why: Romeo and Juliet was written and structured as a tragedy from the outset, following the genre's conventions of a fatal flaw or circumstance leading to the protagonists' deaths — this was Shakespeare's deliberate design, not a later mislabel.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: a student thinks the prologue's sonnet form is just a poetic decoration with no real purpose. what does the sonnet form actually signal to the audience
options: it signals the play's tragic outcome and love theme upfront, setting audience expectations
it signals the play is actually a comedy despite what happens later
it has no connection to the play's plot or themes at all
it was only included to fill time before the actors were ready
questions.answer: it signals the play's tragic outcome and love theme upfront, setting audience expectations
questions.why: The prologue's sonnet form, with its formal structure, immediately tells the audience this is a love story that ends in tragedy ('star-crossed lovers take their life'), framing expectations before the plot even begins.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: your friend says the crusades don't matter much to modern students because they were fought over religion, and religion-based conflicts aren't relevant to studying today's world. explain to your friend why understanding the crusades still helps us understand conflicts and connections in the modern world.
